authorship.what_this_is: The single generation attempt for each frozen-five opportunity whose supplied contrast set reached a solvable V2 blueprint. Only G2-PED-01 did. The stem realizes that blueprint exactly and states nothing else; distractor option text is the frozen curated seed string verbatim.
authorship.rationale_rule: A distractor rationale may say a condition is contradicted by the stem only where the stem states the contrary or the frozen contradiction list entails it. Where a condition is simply unreported, the rationale says so and rests on the cited discriminator instead. The V1 template clause 'That condition is not met here' does not appear.
authorship.review_independence_limit: The blind solve and the admissibility review were run as separate blinded passes by the same model instance rather than by independent agents. That is a weaker form of independence than the three fresh reviewers of the contrast-first pilot, and it is stated rather than glossed.

G2-PED-01.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?
G2-PED-01.stem: A 7-month-old girl is brought to hospital. Three days ago she developed clear nasal discharge, sneezing and a cough, and yesterday she began to wheeze for the first time in her life. She has been treated for atopic dermatitis since the age of two months. On examination her respiratory rate is 62 breaths per minute, she has subcostal and intercostal indrawing, and wheeze is audible on auscultation. Her work of breathing has increased over the two hours since arrival and the team is considering high-flow nasal cannula support.

stem_feature_map.source_span: She has been treated for atopic dermatitis since the age of two months
yesterday she began to wheeze for the first time in her life
Her work of breathing has increased over the two hours since arrival and the team is considering high-flow nasal cannula support
Three days ago she developed clear nasal discharge, sneezing and a cough

G2-PED-01.key_rationale: CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR states that bronchiolitis typically presents with a first episode of wheezing before the age of twelve months, beginning with a two-to-three-day viral prodrome, and CLM-GEN-PED-DX-01 makes typical bronchiolitis a clinical diagnosis in an otherwise healthy child of this age. All three of those conditions are stated here: seven months old, a three-day coryzal illness, and a first wheeze.

distractor_rationales.SEED-PED-T01-ASTHMA: Plausible: documented atopy is one of the features CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL names as a reason to consider a broader differential, and CLM-R2-PED-DDX-TABLE places asthma first among the conditions to distinguish from bronchiolitis. Inferior: its own condition begins with an older infant or child, and the stem states an age of seven months, which is contrary to that precondition.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PED-T01-FOREIGN-BODY: Plausible: escalating work of breathing is the atypical presentation CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL says should prompt the broad differential of CLM-R2-PED-DDX-TABLE, which contains aspiration. Inferior: aspiration is correct where onset was abrupt without a preceding viral illness, and the stem states a three-day coryzal prodrome, which is the contrary of that. The stem does not report whether the chest findings are focal or asymmetric; it is not claimed here that they are not, and on CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR the prodrome-to-first-wheeze course under twelve months is the bronchiolitis pattern.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PED-T01-PNEUMONIA: Plausible: the same sentence of CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL and the same differential table, in which pneumonia sits directly opposite bronchiolitis. Inferior: its conditions are that the illness is not improving as expected, that severity raises a specific concern for bacterial infection, or that a focal consolidation is demonstrated. The stem reports none of the three, in either direction, and this item does not assert that they are absent. What it does state is the pattern CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR describes, and under a most-likely lead-in that pattern is what decides the answer.

G2-PED-01.reasoning: Seven months old, a three-day coryzal illness, then a first-ever wheeze with increasing work of breathing. That is the bronchiolitis course. Asthma is the option the atopic dermatitis is pulling towards, but a first wheeze at seven months is not a first presentation of asthma. Aspiration is argued against by the three days of coryza before the wheeze rather than an abrupt onset. Pneumonia is not excluded by anything stated, but nothing stated points to it either, and the lead-in asks for the most likely diagnosis rather than the only possible one.
G2-PED-01.difficulty_comment: Every one of the key's conditions is stated in the stem in plain words and the competing option that shares an anchor is defeated by a stated age. The only work is to resist the atopic dermatitis, which is one step.

G2-PED-01.comment: A natural paediatric vignette that reads as a real presentation rather than an assembled checklist: a seven-month-old with three days of coryza, a first wheeze, and rising work of breathing. Four options, four distinct mechanisms, no overlap. The respiratory rate is appropriate for the age and no number is asserted that the evidence does not carry. The rationales are the strongest part of the item: two of the three decline in terms to convert the stem's silence into a denial, which is the defect that sank most of the V1 arm.
observations: The item is declared MEDIUM and reads EASY. Every key condition is stated verbatim and the only integration required is to weigh a stated age against a stated atopy. This is the same tension the pilot already recorded for G2-PHELO-03: the completeness that makes an item safe is what makes it read easy.

The weakest link is that two of the three competitors, foreign body aspiration and pneumonia, are made live by the same feature, escalating work of breathing. It is a cited anchor -- CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL names severe respiratory distress as the presentation that should prompt the broad differential in which both sit -- and it is a real finding rather than stem furniture, so it is not scored as a defect. But it is a generic severity feature doing plausibility work for two options at once, and a reviewer who wanted to fail this item would fail it there.

Pneumonia is settled by a discriminator over three unreported conditions rather than by a stated contrary. Under a most-likely lead-in that is sound, because an unreported condition does not make a competitor co-correct. Under a 'which of the following is excluded' lead-in it would not be.
